place: Kathmandu — Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple) and Durbar Square
message: Rest day in Kathmandu. Tyler explored Swayambhunath — the Monkey Temple — and Durbar Square this morning, then headed back to the hotel to relax before walking around Thamel in the afternoon. The trek begins tomorrow.

photos.caption: Sunset over Kathmandu from the Monkey Temple hill.
A mother monkey grooming her baby at sunset.
The Swayambhunath stupa, its Buddha eyes watching over the city.
The long staircase climb up to the temple.
A row of prayer wheels at the temple.
A street dog catching a nap on a brick step.

message: Guided tour of Durbar Square with Mr Chet, who taught Tyler about Nepali culture and history — Kathmandu means "wooden city" (many original temples built mainly of wood, some from a single tree) and Nepal means "adopted by guru" — and treated him to a traditional Nepali breakfast for $1. Mr Chet invited him to celebrate the end of Dashain with his family after the trek. A fun, busy start to the day before tomorrow's flight to Lukla.

message: Day 1 of the trek is underway! Tyler flew into Lukla this morning and trekked on to Monjo, arriving at his lodge this afternoon. The Himalayan adventure has officially begun. Day 1 by the numbers (per his Garmin): 7.82 miles, 2,090 ft of elevation gain, 3 hours 40 minutes — “endless ups and downs, countless donkeys and yaks (and their poop), but also so many beautiful views.”

photos.caption: Snow-capped Himalayan peaks from the plane window.
The Lukla runway at Tenzing-Hillary Airport, mountains all around.
Tyler crossing a suspension bridge on the trail.
Stone lodges along the trail with the mountains behind.
The main dining area at the Monjo lodge.
The dining room stove keeping things cozy.

The view from Tyler's room.

message: Day 2 done — Tyler made it to Namche! He trekked up from Monjo, crossing the Dudh Koshi on its long suspension bridges (a little nerve-wracking, especially sharing them with the mule trains) and passing through the Sagarmatha National Park gate along the way. He is settled at the Panorama Lodge overlooking Namche for the next two nights. He met Anna and Frank, an older couple from the Netherlands, and they bonded over Holland — both the Michigan and European kind. Pulse ox was 94% on arrival and he says he feels really strong physically. Day 2 by the numbers (per his Garmin): 3.84 miles, 2,487 ft of elevation gain, 2 hours 12 minutes — a “crazy steep day” with plenty of breaks for water, waiting for the mules (or are they donkeys?) at the suspension bridges, and admiring the views.

photos.caption: The Dudh Koshi river in all its might.
Taboche peak through the valley.
Tyler at a viewpoint with Taboche behind.
One of the long suspension bridges over the Dudh Koshi.
Tyler entering Sagarmatha National Park.

message: Acclimatization day! Tyler was up and hiking at 6am, beating the breakfast crowds to have Hotel Everest View (3,880m) nearly to himself. A couple of energy snacks held him over for the climb, with a proper breakfast waiting at the viewpoint — plus coffee at 3,880 meters. Lhotse and Ama Dablam played peek-a-boo through the clouds. The climb up took an hour flat (1.91 miles, 1,339 ft of elevation gain) — “coffee and a view.” The hike back down was “so beautiful,” and spotting some of the BIG ones has him excited for the days ahead.

photos.caption: Lhotse partially hidden behind the clouds.
Ama Dablam peeking through the clouds.
Coffee at 3,880 meters!
The entrance to Hotel Everest View (3,880m).

message: Day 4: Namche → Tengboche. The morning started with a breakfast view from the Panorama Lodge — snow-dusted peaks over Namche’s blue rooftops. With Tengboche fully booked, the plan was to push on to Pangboche — but a room opened up in Tengboche after all. Mani stone walls, snowy valleys, and a prayer-flagged chorten marked the trail. Day 4 by the numbers (per his Garmin): 6.47 miles, 2,671 ft of elevation gain, 3 hours 26 minutes moving — “one helluva climb the last couple miles,” with mist and sprinkles, but the rain held off.

photos.caption: The breakfast view from the lodge in Namche.
Tyler by a mani stone wall on the trail.
A snowy valley along the way.
A chorten with prayer flags on the trail.

message: Day 5: Tengboche → Dingboche. Bundled up against the morning cold, Tyler set out around 7 for 10km of steady uphill — about the same time on trail as previous days. He picked a good lodge here — a bit more expensive, but with an attached bathroom and shower, a sunroom that gets super warm during the day (prime sunbathing spot), and a very nice hostess and team. The big news: his first glimpse of Everest, peeking out from behind Lhotse’s ridge. Ama Dablam dominated the views all day, and a yak shared the trail. Day 5 by the numbers (per his Garmin): 6.40 miles, 2,270 ft of elevation gain, 3 hours 5 minutes — “absolutely beautiful day, not a cloud in the sky,” Everest, Lhotse and Ama Dablam all in view, and the body still holding up well.

photos.caption: Bundled up for the cold morning departure from Tengboche — the face covering gives sun protection and warms and moistens the thin air.
First glimpse of Everest, peeking from behind Lhotse’s ridge (Lhotse on the right).
Tyler with Ama Dablam behind.

A chorten with Ama Dablam rising behind it. The Eyes of Buddha gaze out in the four directions — a symbol of the Buddha's all-seeing wisdom, watchfulness, and compassion for the world. The curl between them is the Nepali character for 'one,' a reminder that everything is connected.
On the trail with Ama Dablam ahead.
Mani stones and cairns on the way to Dingboche.
A yak on the trail.

message: Day 6: acclimatization day in Dingboche — and what a day. Tyler climbed to Ngargjung, a 16,600-foot summit above the village: “The views are unreal and I feel so blessed to be here.” Prayer flags at the top, Ama Dablam in black and white, glacier-carved valleys, and Dingboche spread out below. The descent was a careful one — the trail turned muddy as the sun came up, so he took it slow. “A tough climb but I still felt really good in general — it’s giving me a lot of confidence for these next few days.” Back at the lodge: the green-roofed one, with Ama Dablam towering right behind it. Day 6 by the numbers (per his Garmin): 3.59 miles, 2,795 ft of elevation gain, 2 hours 41 minutes — “higher than any point in the continental US,” lungs and legs still holding up fine, and going back down tougher than going up.

message:
Day 7, part 1: Dingboche → Chukhung — “super chill hike, lots of half tundra half wetlands which was neat.” 3.50 miles, 1,627 ft of elevation gain, 1 hour 48 minutes.

Part 2: Chukhung → Chukhung Ri — the highest elevation he’ll hit on the whole trek. “Brutal climb. Worth the suffering. Legs are fried but will be good to go tomorrow. Pass looks good.” 4.23 miles, 3,009 ft of elevation gain, 3 hours 5 minutes.
